mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLE 350d or 400d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM642 engine for the GLE 350d costs £3,500-£4,500 supply-only; a rebuilt OM656 engine for the GLE 400d costs £5,500-£6,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - the OM656's inline-six is more accessible than the OM642's V6.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM642 oil cooler seal failure on a Mercedes GLE 350d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A burning oil smell from the engine bay is the classic warning sign. Oil leaks from the V of the engine onto the exhaust. If ignored, oil loss can cause bottom-end failure. The original orange seals were replaced with updated purple seals from approximately 2010.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLE 400d engine (OM656) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 inline-six is a modern, powerful diesel with excellent performance - 330hp and 700Nm torque. However, it has a known EGR cooler issue that prompted safety recalls, as well as AdBlue system problems. With recalls addressed and proper maintenance, these engines are proving durable.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLE 350d and 400d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 V6 diesels routinely reach 150,000-200,000+ miles before major work. The OM656 inline-six is too new for definitive long-term data, but with recalls addressed, similar longevity is expected.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLE 350d or 400d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLE is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £3,500-£4,500 - far less than replacing a £12,000-£22,000 vehicle. The GLE 400d's higher value (£25,000-£45,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLE 350d or 400d need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres; the OM656 inline-six requires approximately 8.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 350d/400d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLE 350d launched with the W166 generation in 2015, powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel - a proven workhorse delivering 258hp and effortless torque. In 2019, the W167 GLE 400d replaced it with the all-new OM656 2.9-litre inline-six diesel - more powerful, more refined, and built on an entirely new engine architecture that brought both performance gains and new technical challenges.

items.title: 3.0L V6 Diesel (2015-2019)
items.commonFailure: Oil cooler seal degradation - the seals in the V of the engine degrade over time, allowing oil to leak onto the exhaust and produce a burning smell. The original orange seals were replaced with updated purple seals from approximately 2010 onwards. Turbo oil seal failure is also common, with oil leaking onto the swirl flap motor. Typical failure mileage: 70,000-110,000 miles.

items.title: 2.9L Inline-Six Diesel (2019-present)
items.commonFailure: EGR cooler internal coolant leakage - a known issue affecting OM656 engines. Over time, the EGR cooler can develop an internal coolant leak, allowing coolant to mix with diesel soot particles, which can damage the engine intake manifold and increase the risk of fire. A safety recall was issued for OM654 and OM656 diesel engines. Coolant pump vacuum circuit leaks have also been reported, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum system. Typical failure mileage: 40,000-70,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLE Class 350d/400d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLE 350d's OM642 V6 and the GLE 400d's OM656 inline-six are both fundamentally robust diesel engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that drive replacement decisions. The OM642's V6 suffers from oil cooler seal failures - a £10 part that costs £1,000 in labour to replace. The OM656's EGR cooler has been subject to safety recalls. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM642 Oil Cooler & Turbo Oil Seal Failure
problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler & Turbo Oil Seal Failure - The V6 Diesel's Expensive Weakness
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler sits in the V of the engine. The original orange seals degrade over time, allowing oil to leak onto the exhaust and produce a burning smell. The turbo oil seal can also leak onto the swirl flap motor below. Older orange seals were replaced with updated purple seals from approximately 2010 onwards, but failures still occur on later examples.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, injectors, wiring harness to access V of engine; replace seals with updated purple units
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbocharger, oil feed lines, gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo seal has failed causing smoking exhaust

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 with upgraded seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil loss has caused bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2019 GLE 350d 4MATIC is worth approximately £12,000-£22,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLE 350d sits in the £8,000-£15,000 to £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples.
problems.recommendation: If you smell burning oil from the engine bay of your GLE 350d, act immediately. The OM642's V-design makes accessing the oil cooler seals labour-intensive - but £1,000 at a specialist is significantly cheaper than the £3,500+ full replacement. The updated purple seals are more durable than the original orange items. On a GLE 350d worth £12,000-£22,000, a £1,000 specialist seal replacement is excellent preventative maintenance.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes GLE 350d engine prices

problems.h4: OM656 EGR Cooler Failure - The Inline-Six Diesel's Recall Crisis
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop an internal coolant leak. If coolant mixes with diesel soot particles, this can damage the engine intake manifold and increase the risk of a fire. A safety recall affects OM654 and OM656 diesel engines. Coolant pump vacuum circuit leaks have also been reported, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Mercedes dealer inspection and replacement under recall
repairOptions.longevity: Check your VIN immediately on Mercedes recall portal

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler unit, coolant flush, gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: If recall doesn't apply or work not yet performed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 with updated EGR cooler, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If EGR failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-present GLE 400d 4MATIC is worth approximately £25,000-£45,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLE 400d sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: Check your VIN immediately for any outstanding OM656 EGR cooler recalls. If the recall has been performed and you're still experiencing issues, specialist EGR cooler replacement at £500-£750 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. However, if the engine has overheated due to coolant loss from a failed cooler, a full rebuilt OM656 is the only safe option - on a GLE 400d worth £25,000-£45,000, this is a justifiable investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM656 Mercedes GLE 400d engine prices

problems.h4: OM656 AdBlue & SCR System Problems - Emissions Compliance Issues
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue system on OM656 engines can suffer from crystallisation in the injector nozzle, NOx sensor failures, and SCR system malfunctions. The AdBlue system is "the biggest problem with most Merc diesels" and can be very expensive to repair. Type of driving doesn't appear to make a difference.

repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; only suitable for light crystallisation

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue injector, flush tank and lines, reset SCR counter
repairOptions.longevity: If injector is blocked beyond cleaning

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both upstream and downstream NOx sensors
repairOptions.longevity: If sensor failure causing emissions warnings

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 with new AdBlue components
repairOptions.longevity: If AdBlue/SCR issues have caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical GLE 400d is worth £25,000-£45,000.
problems.recommendation: The AdBlue system on OM656 engines is notoriously problematic. Use only high-quality AdBlue from reputable sources - buying from petrol stations or discount stores "will probably lead to issues". If you experience emissions warnings, have a specialist perform diagnostics immediately. Replacing the AdBlue injector and both NOx sensors as a pair is often the most cost-effective approach, preventing repeat workshop visits. Some owners choose to delete the entire system, but this is illegal.
